title: GPU pool pulse — morning notes
content:
Morning pulse — quick brain dump (Riley)

Context: wallet of GPU pools (dev/dedicated/spot-burst). Running small experiment today to stress autoscaler and reclaim script. Short notes so I don't forget mid-shift.

Goals for today:
- Validate reclaim script on non-prod pool with 72h idle threshold (dry-run first).
- Confirm network MTU glitch on h100 cluster doesn't regress after kernel update.
- Push tiny autoscale tuning: decrease cpuThreshold for infer-frontend from 0.55 -> 0.45 in canary zone.
- Finish writeup for INFRA-2419 with numbers from yesterday's run.

Morning checklist (quick run):
- [ ] kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide (check nodeReady, kernel, taints)
- [ ] nvidia-smi loop on node-0 (top 3 pods), record mem/util snapshot: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 5 > /tmp/gpu-snap.csv
- [ ] curl to /health on inference router (canary + primary)
- [ ] Check monitoring: grafana - token_events (p99 latency), gpu_utilization pool h100-a100 comparison

Observations from 07:30 quick pass:
- Node group h100-eu-west-2 shows 18% idle GPU time across nodes 12-17 between 02:00-06:00 UTC. Suspect some v2 batch workload not cleaned up.
- One node (h100-eu-14) had a kubelet restart at 03:42, dmesg shows network timeout while kube-proxy reloaded. Need logs: kubectl -n kube-system logs kube-proxy-h100-eu-14
- Reclaim dry-run yesterday flagged 9 long-idle pods (labels: job=auto-infer-test). All from team:solutions-eng sandbox. Need to send heads-up before actual deletion.

Quick commands / snippets (save here so I don't open terminals repeatedly):
- List GPU nodes: kubectl get nodes -l node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,INST:.metadata.labels.instance-type,AGE:.metadata.creationTimestamp
- Check pod GPU allocation: kubectl get pods -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU:.spec.resources.requests.nvidia\.com/gpu -n inference
- Reclaim dry-run: python infra/scripts/reclaim.py --pool h100-eu --dry-run --min-idle-hours 72 --output /tmp/reclaim-dryrun.json
- Grab kubelet logs last 4h: journalctl -u kubelet --since "4 hours ago" | gzip -c > /tmp/kubelet-eu14.log.gz

Immediate TODO (priority order):
1) Reclaim dry-run review (Maya) — run list through 1:1 with solutions-eng owners before actual run. (blocker: owners not mapped for 3 pods)
2) Investigate kernel/net upgrade rollback on h100-eu-14 (Theo to look infra side, Riley to gather dmesg)
3) Canary scale tweak (apply to canary ASG, watch p99 for 15m, then roll): change cpuThreshold 0.55 -> 0.45; rollout plan notes in PR #1234
4) Confirm HSM KMS rotation didn't touch instance profile keys yesterday (double-check with security)

Background numbers (last 24h):
- Total GPUs (all pools): 214 (a100: 112, h100: 78, t4/equiv: 24)
- Avg GPU utilization (24h): 63% overall; peak window 12:30-13:10 UTC at 92% on service=chatgen-v2
- Idle GPU pool fraction: 9.1% (targets: <5% for prod)
- Reclaim candidates (72h idle): 13 pods flagged, 9 confirmed dev/workbench, 4 uncertain (need owner mapping)

Open questions / parking lot:
- Should we auto-scale down reserved Dedicated pools during low-util business hours? (legal/commit constraints?)
- Is the MTU mismatch an underlying CNI plugin bug or kernel regression from the security team update?
- Would conservative GPU overcommit help cost without harming latency for batched workloads? Quick simulation needed.

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Ping @m.ortiz in #infra-gpu-ops with reclaim list + ask owners to annotate. Template: "hi — flagged X pods in your namespace as idle >72h; please confirm keep/delete by EOD or we'll schedule reclaim next maintenance window"
- Add small snippet to runbook: how to toggle debug level for kube-proxy and capture pcap quickly. Keep as single-command alias on jumpbox.
- Draft the INFRA-2419 comment with pool numbers and proposed schedule for reclaim (two-week ramp, initial dry-run, owner opt-out form).

End-of-shift quick state (what to leave for next person):
- Reclaim dry-run file: /tmp/reclaim-dryrun.json (shared with Maya)
- Canary PR #1234 pending review from SRE (Theo) — merge only after 15m stable in canary
- Node h100-eu-14: logs collected /tmp/kubelet-eu14.log.gz; leave node cordoned until root cause known (sre@ oncall notified)

Random ideas / low-priority experiments (parking lot):
- Small experiment: run a 1-hr micro-benchmark with model q4_K_Mixed on a100 vs h100 to measure per-token latency and memory pressure; use that to update recommend quant profiles in optimize tool.
- Add owner tag enforcement in CI for ephemeral sandbox namespaces so reclaim has owner metadata. Could be a GitHub Action that fails namespace creation without owner label.

Scratch: half-remembered ticket/links to add to write-up:
- INFRA-2419 (pool sizing) — need to attach reclaim dry-run numbers
- PR 1234 (autoscale tweak) — add rs entries for rollout history
- Confluence: GPU Pool Sizing Notes (summary table)

-- Riley

(End of dump)
